newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia financiers warn of "harmful" defense cuts.
newsitem.headline: Colombia financiers warn of "harmful" defense cuts.

text.p: The Colombian government is diverting vital funds away from the war against leftist guerrillas in order to plug its gaping fiscal deficit, an influential financial group warned Sunday.

In its weekly report the National Association of Financial Institutions (ANIF) criticized the government for "inefficient" and "harmful" public spending programs and called on it to reverse a decision, announced last week, to slash more than $120 million from the defense budget.
It also warned that an additional $440 million in military spending, which the government is looking to raise from the sale of "war bonds" to rich Colombians, could be used for non-defense purposes.
"There was always the fear that (military) resources would be used to cover the fiscal deficit and therefore not used on defense spending. Unfortunately that is now happening," the report said.
"And despite the promises of top officials, a substantial part of the war bonds income will be diverted to filling the black holes of public finances," it added.

The government announced last month it would cut a total 1.3 trillion pesos from an overall budget of about 30 trillion pesos as part of it plan to rein in a fiscal deficit that reached four percent of gross domestic product (GDP) in 1996.

Representatives of Colombia's financial and business elite have, however, argued that more should be spent on counterinsurgency operations to combat one of the biggest guerrilla offensives in three decades of armed uprising.
The government originally planned to spend more than $900 million on defense in 1997 -- more than the combined military expenditure for the last four years.
